 Meet the mosquitoes behind Tampa Bay’s dengue outbreak
 The mosquitoes are resilient, love people and could be in your yard.     .   The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which can carry viruses like dengue and Zika, prefers urban areas rather than living in swamps or the woods. The mosquito is driving the spread of dengue in Florida, especially in Tampa Bay, where there have been hundreds of cases and at least one death this year. The mosquitos often lay their eggs in containers like watering cans and flower pots near homes. [ TACIO PHILIP SANSONOVSKI | Dreamstime ] Michaela Mulligan is a climate and environment reporter.
